## 8. Models

<!-- models:start (generated by tools/process_models.mjs; edit outside these markers) -->

### Tilt-Shift (`lumenary:tilt-shift`, models this process)

_From: View cameras and architectural photography; when: Lenses from the 1900s, miniature effect from the 2000s; works best on: High-angle city, harbour and crowd scenes._

A tilt-shift lens tips its plane of focus so that only a thin band is sharp and the rest falls quickly into blur. That is also what happens when you photograph a tiny scene up close, so a street photographed this way tricks the brain into seeing a model. Boosted colour and contrast add the gloss of a toy.

**How it is made, as the model does it:**

1. Build five versions of the picture in advance, with blur radii of 0, 1.6, 3.6, 7 and 12 pixels scaled by the blur slider.
2. For each pixel measure its distance from the band: a straight line through the focus point, tilted by the angle slider, or an ellipse for the radial shape.
3. Pass the distance through a smoothstep that starts at the band’s half width and ends further on, scaled to a position among the five levels.
4. Mix the two nearest levels linearly so blur grows smoothly.
5. Raise saturation and contrast, up to 1.85 and 1.45 times, for the look of glossy paint.

**The maths:**

$$t=4\,\operatorname{smoothstep}\!\Big(h,\ h+0.38\,H,\ \big\lvert(\mathbf x-\mathbf c)\cdot\mathbf n\big\rvert\Big),\qquad \mathbf n=(-\sin\alpha,\ \cos\alpha)$$

_Position along the blur levels; h is half the band width, c the focus point, α the tilt. For the radial shape the distance is √((1.15 Δx)² + Δy²)._ (primitives: soft-threshold)

$$C=(1-\phi)\,B_{\lfloor t\rfloor}+\phi\,B_{\lfloor t\rfloor+1},\qquad \phi=t-\lfloor t\rfloor$$

_B₀ is the sharp picture, B₁ to B₄ the blurred ones._ (primitives: blur)

$$C'=\tfrac12+k_c\Big(l+k_s\,(C-l)-\tfrac12\Big)$$

_The model-making boost: saturation k_s and contrast k_c._ (primitives: saturation-adjust, tone-curve)

**Dials:** `focus` (Where the sharp band sits) = 60 [0 to 100]; `width` (Width of the band) = 18 [4 to 60]; `blur` (Blur strength) = 60 [10 to 100]; `angle` (Tilt the band) = 0 [-45 to 45]; `shape` (Shape) = "line" (line, radial); `sat` (Colour boost) = 55 [0 to 100]; `contrast` (Contrast) = 35 [0 to 100].

**History:** Tilt and shift movements on view cameras were used in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries to control perspective in architecture, using principles described by Theodor Scheimpflug in 1904. In the early 2000s photographers such as Olivo Barbieri used them on cities seen from above, and the miniature look became a popular effect in photography and video.
